statement: Adapting selling behavior to the customer and situation is associated with better salesperson performance across the settings synthesized in the cited meta-analysis.
source_locators: Journal of Marketing Research 43(4), pp. 693-702
limitations: Association does not prescribe one universal script
Effect varies by context and seller capability

statement: Salesperson listening is linked to adaptive selling and relational outcomes, but much of the underlying sales evidence is observational.
source_locators: Meta-analytic model and discussion
limitations: Meta-analysis combines heterogeneous measures
Do not infer that listening alone causes conversion

statement: In experimental conversations, asking more questions—especially follow-up questions—can increase how much the conversation partner likes the question asker.
source_locators: JPSP 113(3), pp. 430-452; experiments on follow-up questions
limitations: Liking is not sales conversion
Question quality and relevance still matter

statement: Active empathetic listening can be operationalized as sensing, processing, and responding rather than merely remaining silent.
source_locators: Psychology & Marketing 23, pp. 161-180; three-dimensional scale
limitations: Scale validation is not proof that every listening behavior improves outcomes

statement: Perspective taking improved the discovery of underlying interests and negotiation outcomes in the cited controlled negotiation studies.
source_locators: Psychological Science 19, pp. 378-384
limitations: Negotiation experiments are not direct cold-call replications
Perspective taking must generate hypotheses, not claims about the prospect

statement: High-quality listening can improve interpersonal perceptions and reduce defensiveness without necessarily adding a persuasive effect.
source_locators: PNAS 122(8), preregistered field experiment results
limitations: Political persuasion context differs from B2B sales
Listening remains valuable for understanding even without incremental persuasion

statement: The SPIN framework proposes moving from situation and problem questions toward implications and the value of solving the problem.
source_locators: SPIN method overview
MIT Entrepreneurial Sales curriculum map
limitations: Practitioner framework
Do not force a rigid sequence

statement: Negotiation practice recommends clarifying interests and constraints before arguing over a stated position.
source_locators: Harvard PON research and teaching resource map
Never Split the Difference method overview
limitations: Collection- and practitioner-level synthesis pending asset-specific review

statement: Offer framing should connect the proposed outcome to the prospect's specific constraints rather than reciting generic product features.
source_locators: $100M Offers training map
Adaptive-selling meta-analysis
limitations: Practitioner offer framework
Specific causal claims require Pinkall experiments

statement: Relevant social proof can reduce uncertainty only when it is truthful, comparable, and not presented as a guarantee.
source_locators: Social proof principle overview
limitations: Never fabricate customer names, outcomes, or prevalence
Effect depends on relevance and credibility

statement: A concise paraphrase followed by a confirmation question is an observable way to test whether the listener understood the speaker.
source_locators: Active empathetic listening responding dimension
Salesperson listening meta-analytic discussion
limitations: Paraphrase quality matters
Do not mimic the prospect mechanically

statement: A sales recommendation should be withheld when the transcript and CRM context do not support its triggering interpretation.
source_locators: Adaptive-selling context dependence
Perspective-taking versus unverified empathy distinction
limitations: Pinkall policy synthesis rather than a directly tested intervention

statement: In a new-car-buyer survey model, higher perceived salesperson listening was associated with greater trust and stronger anticipation of future interaction.
source_locators: Abstract and Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science 25(2), pp. 127-137
limitations: Cross-sectional perceived-behavior model does not establish causality
New-car retail buyers are not B2B cold-call prospects
A later exploratory sales study did not reproduce the future-interaction result

statement: Sales listening can be assessed as attending to the message, evaluating or processing it, and responding, but self-report scores are not direct proof of behavior in a recorded call.
source_locators: Ramsey and Sohi abstract: sensing, evaluating, and responding dimensions
Castleberry et al., pp. 30-38: 14-item ILPS scale validation with 604 salespeople
limitations: The validated ILPS instrument is self-reported rather than behaviorally coded
Dimensions do not define a universal composite score for Pinkall

statement: In one B2B buyer sample, listening facets contributed differently to imagery and transactional value, arguing against treating every listening behavior as one interchangeable score.
source_locators: Industrial Marketing Management 98, pp. 222-240, abstract and PLS-SEM results
limitations: Single large US manufacturing-firm buyer sample
Cross-sectional PLS-SEM cannot prove that changing one call behavior creates value
Abstract-level evidence does not support a precise live utterance

statement: In an initial-interaction experiment, paraphrasing the speaker and, when appropriate, inviting elaboration produced greater felt understanding than advice or simple acknowledgements.
source_locators: International Journal of Listening 28(1), pp. 13-31; Experimental Stimuli and Hypothesis Testing sections
limitations: Participants were mainly undergraduates speaking with trained confederates
The experiment measured felt understanding, not sales conversion
Active listening did not outperform advice on conversation satisfaction or social attractiveness

statement: Across motivational-interviewing studies, MI-consistent skills correlated with both change talk and sustain talk; sustain talk, not change talk alone, was the more consistent adverse-outcome signal in separate-path analyses.
source_locators: PubMed abstract results, Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology 86(2), pp. 140-157
limitations: Clinical behavior-change corpus, not selling
Process correlations do not establish that a particular sales question improves conversion
More prospect language is not automatically favorable language

statement: In 62 real B2B encounters led by sales students, buyer-rated questioning skill was associated with purchase intention, but the composite combined need discovery, open questions, probing, and active listening.
source_locators: pp. 3-5, Table 1 questioning items, Table 2 correlations, and OLS results
limitations: Small sample of sales students and low-value advertising products
Composite scale prevents attribution to open questions alone
Customer intention is not an observed purchase and the design is not causal

statement: In contentious written discussions, a recipe using positive statements, explicit acknowledgment, genuine points of agreement, and calibrated hedging improved perceived receptiveness and collaboration evaluations.
source_locators: pp. 139-142, Studies 4a-4b receptiveness recipe; p. 139 lists the four linguistic markers
limitations: Most intervention evidence used written policy disagreement rather than spoken sales calls
Outcomes were receptiveness, cooperation, conflict, and persuasion rather than conversion
Agreement must be genuine and hedging must not weaken required factual clarity

statement: In two negotiation experiments, seeking or providing information about underlying interests improved counterpart-judgment accuracy and joint integrative outcomes, even when only one negotiator did it.
source_locators: Journal of Experimental Social Psychology 27(2), pp. 161-179, abstract and Experiments 1-2
limitations: Controlled negotiation exercises are not cold calls
Integrative joint outcomes are not equivalent to seller revenue
Information must concern interests rather than pressure for positional concessions

statement: Prosocial rather than egoistic negotiation motives were linked to less contention, more problem solving, and higher joint outcomes only when resistance to yielding was high or unknown, not low.
source_locators: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 78(5), pp. 889-905, abstract and moderator analysis
limitations: Social motive is not a directly observable sentence
Effects varied with study design and handling of no-agreement dyads
No evidence supports forcing a problem-solving script when resistance is low

statement: Across reactance studies, the best-fitting model treated anger and counterarguments together as indicators of psychological reactance rather than as independent proof that an objection is genuine.
source_locators: Human Communication Research 39(1), pp. 47-73, abstract and competing-model analysis
limitations: Meta-analysis validated a construct model rather than a sales intervention
Speech emotion inference is uncertain and must not diagnose a prospect
A counterargument may be substantive rather than reactance

statement: In two controlled health-message experiments, perceived threat to freedom affected attitudes and intentions through a combined anger-and-negative-cognition response.
source_locators: Communication Monographs 72(2), pp. 144-168, abstract and parallel experiment path models
limitations: Student health-persuasion context rather than B2B sales
The study does not directly validate any Pinkall autonomy-restoring phrase
Do not infer reactance from a single negative word

statement: Across 94 independent tests, implementation intentions that specified when, where, and how to act had a medium-to-large average effect on a person's own goal attainment.
source_locators: Advances in Experimental Social Psychology 38, pp. 69-119, abstract and meta-analytic discussion
limitations: Most studies were not B2B and did not involve dyadic commercial commitments
Planning supports an existing goal; it does not create consent or genuine intent
A seller-authored next step is not equivalent to the prospect's own implementation intention

statement: In a large randomized phone campaign, helping contacted people form a concrete voting plan increased turnout, while standard encouragement and self-prediction did not; effects differed sharply by household context.
source_locators: Psychological Science 21(2), pp. 194-199, abstract and treatment-effect results
limitations: Voting behavior and campaign calls differ from B2B buying
The 4.1-point estimate applied to people reached, not the full assigned sample
The intervention had no detected effect in multiple-eligible-voter households

statement: In an employee field experiment, prompting people to write a vaccination date and time increased observed follow-through more reliably than an information-only reminder or a date-only prompt.
source_locators: PNAS 108(26), pp. 10415-10420, abstract and regression-adjusted results
limitations: Free on-site vaccination for employees is not a sales follow-up
The date-only any-location estimate was not conventionally significant
Observed effect does not justify pressuring a prospect into a calendar slot

statement: Across question-behaviour studies, asking intention or self-prediction questions had a small average effect on later behavior, and estimates were smaller in better-controlled studies.
source_locators: European Review of Social Psychology, abstract and random-effects meta-analysis: g = 0.14, 95% CI 0.11-0.18
limitations: Heterogeneous behaviors and study designs, mostly outside sales
Small pooled effect is not a license to treat a verbal answer as commitment
A concrete implementation plan is a different intervention from self-prediction

statement: SAMHSA guidance operationalizes motivational interviewing with open questions, affirmations, reflections, and summaries, while warning against moving to action before readiness is explored.
source_locators: TIP 35, Chapter 3, OARS sections and opening strategies
limitations: Institutional clinical practice guidance, not a controlled B2B sales study
Pinkall may borrow observable communication form, not therapeutic positioning
No claim of improved conversion follows from OARS alone

statement: A 2023 exploratory personal-sales study linked salesperson listening with trust and satisfaction but did not find that listening necessarily led to future interaction.
source_locators: International Journal of Knowledge and Learning 16(3), pp. 260-273, abstract and reported outcome pattern
limitations: Exploratory cross-sectional study with setting-specific measurement
Does not show that listening is ineffective for trust or satisfaction
Contrasts with the future-interaction association in Ramsey and Sohi's new-car-buyer sample

statement: Across two customer-service call datasets and four experiments, warmer affective language was more beneficial near the opening and close, while cognitive competence-oriented language was more beneficial in the middle.
source_locators: Journal of Consumer Research 51(3), abstract; field results in Studies 1-2; causal tests in Studies 3-5
limitations: Primary field settings were US customer-service calls rather than cold B2B sales
The authors explicitly identify initial sales calls, culture, issue severity, and conflict as open moderators
Warmth and competence are language categories, not fixed scripts or personality scores

statement: In customer-service field analyses and controlled experiments, relevant concrete language increased perceived listening and customer outcomes; concreteness did not help when the response was irrelevant.
source_locators: Journal of Consumer Research 47(5), abstract; Studies 1-5, especially Study 5 relevance moderation
limitations: Most settings were retail or customer service, not complex B2B buying
Concrete language is not evidence that a factual or commercial claim is true
A specific but irrelevant response can reduce rather than increase perceived listening

statement: In one outbound call-centre field study, sales revenue had an inverted-U association with measured extraversion, consistent with flexible talking and listening rather than maximal assertiveness.
source_locators: Psychological Science 24(6), pp. 1024-1030, abstract and study of 340 outbound representatives
limitations: Single organization and role; personality and speaking behavior were not randomized
The study does not define an optimal talk-listen percentage for an individual call
Revenue association does not prove that changing one conversational turn changes conversion

statement: In two synchronous text-negotiation experiments, early alignment with a counterpart's language improved individual outcomes relative to late alignment or control, with trust mediating one experiment.
source_locators: Journal of Experimental Social Psychology 47(3), pp. 616-621, abstract and Experiments 1-2
limitations: The experiments were text based, not telephone calls
Participants negotiated role-play issues and were not observed in real B2B purchasing
Pinkall must support genuine terminology alignment, never covert imitation of identity, accent, emotion, or protected traits

statement: Once participants were already negotiating, precise opening offers produced counteroffers and settlements closer to the anchor and were perceived as indicating greater knowledge than round offers.
source_locators: Journal of Experimental Social Psychology 49(4), pp. 759-763, Studies 1a-1d, dyadic Study 2, and mechanism Study 3
limitations: Mostly simulated goods negotiations, with one live dyadic experiment
Precision must reflect a real calculation and is not permission to fabricate knowledge
The result changes before negotiation entry, as documented by Lee et al. 2018

statement: Before a counterpart had entered negotiation, precise first offers reduced willingness to engage relative to round offers, mediated by perceptions that the offer maker was inflexible.
source_locators: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes 148, pp. 87-100, abstract; six studies and archival real-estate analysis
limitations: Evidence includes consumer and real-estate contexts rather than SaaS procurement
A round estimate still needs a truthful, internally supported basis
This entry-stage effect does not erase precise anchoring after negotiation begins

statement: Across five controlled social-interaction experiments, participants in voice-only conditions showed higher empathic accuracy than participants in vision-only or multisense conditions.
source_locators: American Psychologist 72(7), pp. 644-654, abstract and Experiments 1-5
limitations: The experiments involved social interactions and recorded strangers, not sales outcomes
A published critical reanalysis disputes the practical magnitude of the reported advantage
Acoustic conditions, language, culture, hearing, and individual expression can all alter vocal cues

statement: A published critical reanalysis of the five voice-only experiments argued that the reported advantage was too small to be practically meaningful.
source_locators: American Psychologist 73(5), pp. 689-690, critical reanalysis comment and abstract
limitations: Published comment and reanalysis, not a new preregistered experiment
The practical-significance threshold is itself an analytic judgment
The critique does not establish that vocal information is always useless

statement: In friendly unstructured conversations, faster partner response times predicted felt connection and experimentally altered third-party connection judgments, but the sub-250 ms effect is not a controllable sales tactic.
source_locators: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 119(4), e2116915119, abstract, Studies 1-3, and limitations
limitations: Samples were friendly conversations between strangers or friends, not goal-directed sales
Negotiation, interview, and conflict were explicitly identified as untested contexts
The timing scale is too fast for deliberate optimization and should not become a performance quota
